chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Zayyāt, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام: A woman saw blood during her menstruation until it passed beyond its usual time; when should she begin to perform salat (prayer)?

He said: She waits for the number of days she used to remain [in menstruation], then she exercises precaution up to ten days. If she sees the blood as flowing blood, then she should perform ghusl (ritual bath) at every time of salat (prayer).

So the correct way regarding his statement عليه السلام, 'she exercises precaution by ten days,' is that we understand it to mean: up to ten days, because that is the maximum number of days of menstruation. Precaution is only required for one day or two days when the habitual period is less than that, and what indicates that is what follows.

key_terms.تَسْتَظْهِرُ: she exercises legal precaution by extending waiting
key_terms.عَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ: ten days, the upper limit referenced here
key_terms.عِدَّتَهَا: the counted number of days of her established habit
key_terms.وَقْتَهَا: its usual appointed time or habitual duration

ai.seo_question: When should a woman begin salat if menstrual bleeding continues beyond her usual habit?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling for a woman whose bleeding continues beyond her normal menstrual period. It explains that she should wait for her established habit, then observe precaution up to ten days, since ten days is the maximum duration of hayd in Shia jurisprudence.
